newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH BGZ BANK TO OPEN MOSCOW OFFICE ON MARCH 20.
newsitem.headline: POLISH BGZ BANK TO OPEN MOSCOW OFFICE ON MARCH 20.

text.p: Poland's Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej SA (BGZ) will open an office in Moscow on March 20, a senior official of the large cooperative bank said on Friday.

"The opening of our office in Moscow will take place next Thursday. It will enable us to provide services to our clients on that market," Antoni Magdon, the president of the bank's supervisory board, told Reuters.
Madgon said the bank, specialising in food-related businesses, would also seek a Russian operating licence.
"Attempts are being made to obtain an operating licence in Russia. We are taking into consideration buying a Russian bank, entering an equity partnership or seeking a licence separately," he said.
Madgon said BGZ estimated that trade with Russia would increase to $4 billion in 1997 from last year's $3 billion.
BGZ would be the fourth Polish bank to open an office in Russia after Pekao SA, Bank Handlowy SA and Kredyt Bank SA.
BGZ's gross profit increased by 37.1 percent to 495.4 million zlotys last year. Its balance sheet total rose 37 percent to nearly 14 billion zlotys.
* Trade on Swiss Options and Financial Futures Exchange (Soffex) concentrated on SMI futures.

SMI futures were easier to trade than the underlying stocks on the cash market, one dealer explained. In all 9,943 SMI future contracts changed hands, of which 8,583 were March futures. The March SMI was up 18.6 to 4,622.6 points.
Volume in options was lower at 109,829 contracts. The call/put ratio was at 1.38 to one.
